{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"FAQPage","@id":"https://signalmash.com/short-code-messaging#faq","mainEntity":[{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I keep my short code if I switch providers?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, short codes are portable. You can transfer a registered short code between providers, ensuring you maintain customer engagement without disruption."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I use a short code for both SMS and MMS?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Short codes support both text messages (SMS) and multimedia messages (MMS), allowing businesses to send images, GIFs, and videos."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Do short codes work internationally?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"In the U.S. and Canada, short codes are country-specific. If you need international short codes, we can help you navigate the approval process in different regions."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How long does it take to set up a short code?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Short code approval can take between 6 to 12 weeks, as carriers review messaging use cases and compliance details."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What industries use short codes?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Short codes are widely used in retail and e-commerce (flash sales, promotions), finance and banking (fraud alerts, account authentication), healthcare (appointment reminders, prescription updates) and government and public safety (emergency notifications)."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How do I get people to opt in for short code messaging?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Businesses must obtain explicit opt-in consent before sending messages. Common methods include website forms, keyword-based opt-ins (e.g., 'Text JOIN to 12345'), and mobile app agreements."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I integrate short code messaging into my CRM or helpdesk?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes. Signalmash provides API and webhook integrations to sync short code messaging with CRM systems, helpdesks, and customer engagement platforms."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Can I set up automated responses on my short code?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Yes, short codes support automated responses based on keywords, triggers, or chatbot interactions, improving customer engagement."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"What is the difference between a short code and 10DLC?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"A short code is a dedicated 5-6 digit number that sends hundreds of messages per second with the highest deliverability, while 10DLC uses a standard 10-digit local number with lower throughput and lower cost. Short codes take 8-12 weeks to approve; 10DLC campaigns take days."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How much does a short code cost?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"In the US a random short code leases for about $500 per month and a vanity short code for about $1,000 per month, billed quarterly by the registry, plus per-message fees. Signalmash also offers shared short code programs for lower-volume senders."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"Does a US short code work in Canada?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"No. US and Canadian short codes are separate programmes with separate carriers, registries and approvals. Sending to both countries means leasing a code in each, or using a verified toll-free number, which delivers to both."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How much does a Canadian short code cost?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"The Canadian Telecommunications Association's published fee is a $1,500 plus tax deposit covering the first three months and $350 plus tax per month after that, on a one-year lease, with a $250 monthly rate for registered charities. Provider platform and per-message fees are additional, and provisioning takes three to six weeks after the weekly application review."}},{"@type":"Question","name":"How do I find out who texted me from a short code?","acceptedAnswer":{"@type":"Answer","text":"Reply HELP to the code: carrier rules require the programme to answer with the brand name and contact details.
